_comment: Which shim dylib each library's load command is repointed to in Phase 5.
Read by scripts/05_retarget.py.
The key is the install name as it appears in Roblox's LC_LOAD_DYLIB (which
is what dyld would look up), and the value is the shim's install name. One
shim per library, because a two-level-namespace import names both a symbol
and the library it must come from: dyld resolves it against that library
and the closure of what that library re-exports, nowhere else.
Only libraries with at least one unresolved non-weak eager import are
listed. A framework that is absent on the device but whose every import is
weak is deliberately NOT repointed: dyld binds a missing weak import to
NULL and the app still loads, and Roblox already has to cope with that on
iOS. Repointing those would add load commands and behaviour for no gain.
That is why DeclaredAgeRange, MarketplaceKit, Social, VisionKit and
libswiftPhotosUI do not appear here despite being absent on the device:
their imports are all weak (33, 9, 3, 1 and 13 symbols respectively).
Proxy (framework is on the device, short a symbol; the shim re-exports the
real library and adds what is missing):
UIKit, CoreFoundation, CoreTelephony, PushKit, libswiftDarwin
Stand-in (framework absent from the device; the shim defines only the
symbols Roblox imports):
MessageUI, SafariServices, PDFKit, WidgetKit, FileProvider and the
libswift{CallKit,CoreMIDI,DataDetection,FileProvider,PassKit} overlays
QuickLook, iAd and EventKitUI are here for a different reason from the
rest: Roblox links all three with a NON-weak LC_LOAD_DYLIB, all three are
absent from the device, and Roblox imports zero symbols from any of them.
They never appeared in missing.json because there was no unresolved symbol
to report -- but dyld requires a non-weak LC_LOAD_DYLIB to be loadable
whether or not anything is imported from it, so they fail the launch before
any Roblox code runs. Their stand-ins define nothing.
